Was having an issue with results changing but suspect this was actually due to loading the wrong file. Will have to do testing to make sure.








For the Random Forest, I have kept results from a previous attempt in which I used the raw next_close as the target. I imputed the implied percentage change from those results, and compared them to the newer version in which NCPC was the target.

The raw target's mean error was 2.19% and the median error was 1.27%.
The pct target's mean error was 0.72% and the median error was 0.38%.

A two-thirds improvment, and without any GridSearch or feature refinement. 

I also attempted a classification model in which I merely predicted whether next_close would be positive or negative. Accuracy was only 50.1%. In my NCPC regression model, 99% of rows were directionally correct.

These figures only confirms my pre-existing conviction that NCPC is the correct target.

I may repeat this comparison with other model types and more advanced models.

(If I want to do more classification/directionality comparison, will have to fix merging. Probably not important for now.)














Should hourly data directly interact with the daily models? To what extent?




Will have to refine my modeling codeblocks to be instantly compatible with multiple feature sets, only changing one line.








I downloaded nearly 6000 stocks from the Massive API. Since such a sized dataset would be impractical to work with, I made a reduced dataset consisting only of stocks with an average of 30000 daily transactions, and with a satisfactorily low number of misisng days, which reduced the stocks to 397. 

Those same 397 stocks have also been downloaded with full hourly data.





My full daily dataset stretches from 2021-05-05 to 2026-05-01.

After calculating SMAs up to 100 days, as well as dropping the final row per ticker for which next_close does not exist, the span is from 2021-07-15 to 2026-04-30.



My plan is to use 2021-2024 data for training, 2025 for testing, and 2026 for validation

I will measure each model by test-validation falloff.





2021 through 2024 will be used as training.

2025 as test.

2026 as validation.






My first models are with the full dataset and all calculated features.
Potentially, another feature set could contain only features correlated to a low error rate.





Eventually, I want to add gap analysis - to see what happened over weekends and holidays.

Out of all my calculated metrics, I'd like to measure each relative to the average of the dataset - but those won't be modeling features.




It was suggested that I could have up to 100 different models, from different combinations of features and model types. Could also optimize for different GridSearch strengths (better recall/precision/F1 etc).

CURRENT IDEA
MODEL FILENAMES WILL BE AS FOLLOWS:

model_,
daily_ or hourly,
model type (such as RFC, XGB etc),
GridSearch optimization (P for precision, R for recall, F for F1, X for no GridSearch)
feature set (featmax = full list of features, feat2 = second list of features - these will be defined elsewhere)

model_daily_rfc_GSX_featmax

May be forced to revise or abandon this level of detail, if n_estimators and such will also be varied.

POTENTIAL PROBLEM -
Daily high, low, open and close match up exactly with what I am seeing for the corresponding day in the hourly dataset. HOWEVER, 'volume' in the daily dataset does not seem to match the sum of all hourly 'volume' values for that day. I was advised that this is to be expected given different methods in gathering data.

If I rescale, I will use daily totals as the "truth" to adjust hourly data to. It might not matter though, since hourly and daily data will likely not be put into the same model.




I find it important to somewhat split up ML commands to avoid a notebook being too long. Normally I do this by making each model its own notebook. However that also gets hard to manage. 

Would it make sense to store commands in txt files and simply load their path in the notebook? Would formatting work?




Want to put more effort into formatting the notebooks this time as well.




Was instructed to use at least one LSTM. Should do more than one.




Should incorporate unsupervised learning as well if possible. For example if I have transactions, let them be sorted and use the assigned categories as features? Is that getting too recursive?






In creating dataframes with daily data, need to add SMA20, SMA50 etc. Need it to happen right out of the box to avoid reprocessing later. If the data includes fewer days than the specified average, take whatever is available. Or could these SMAs be gathered straight from the API?




In measuring daily changes, should also measure across average of all stocks.



Weird, seems AAPL never had a signed daily change of at least 2%. Is AAPL just an unusually stable stock or do I need to find another source?

My plan limits me to five years of data, to the day. Every day, another day of historical data will fall outside my window. I would like to keep data that falls outside the window over the course of the project, but with my current methods, over time this would result in having to create a new CSV every day manually, and then manually combine to remove duplicates. How practical or difficult would it be to set up something like a Webhook to manually grab this data.

My instinct is this doesn't matter much, as long as I have a 5-year window.
